unit.title: From Benchmark to Defensible Claim
unit.scope: A bounded introduction to empirical measurement, paired analysis, reproducible tooling, and appropriately limited claims using an embedded synthetic benchmark dataset.
prerequisites: Ability to write and test a small command-line program
learning_objectives: Translate an algorithm-performance intuition into a precise empirical question and estimand.
Identify observational units, variables, pairing, and threats to validity in benchmark data.
Build a deterministic, tested analysis command with explicit input validation and provenance.
Report heterogeneous results without turning a descriptive observation into a causal or population-wide claim.

unit_completion_requires: All required submission artifacts are present.
The analysis is reproducible from the documented command.
Harness-controlled validation and independent examination pass.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: Completing or validating this kickoff records progress for manager_unit_01_benchmark_to_claim only. It does not mark CMU 17-803, any official CMU assignment, or the catalog course as completed.
completion_policy.later_expansion: Additional units require separately retrieved, classified, provenance-recorded, and validated public materials.

provenance.claims_policy: Catalog claims are retained as source-derived metadata; the kickoff design and synthetic data are new local artifacts and are not represented as official CMU content.
